implementation_notes: Node has no language-level transactions, so the boundary comes from the client library: KafkaJS (Kafka 0.11+) returns a transaction object from producer.transaction(), stages sends made through transaction.send/sendBatch on it, and makes them visible only on transaction.commit() (discarded by transaction.abort()); transaction.sendOffsets() commits consumed offsets inside the same transaction, which closes the consume-transform-produce loop. For the database-coupled case no client spans both resources, so the outbox path applies: write an outbox row inside the pg transaction (BEGIN ... COMMIT on one client) and publish after the transaction resolves, or let a relay publish committed rows.
pitfalls: Forgetting transaction.abort() in the catch leaves the transaction open and later sends fail until the broker times it out.
Sends made through the base producer inside the transaction body are not staged and become visible immediately - the dual-write bug in library form.
Exactly-once needs transactionalId, idempotent: true and maxInFlightRequests: 1 together; without them the producer still sends but loses ordering and fencing guarantees.
The event loop gives no atomicity with a database: an await between COMMIT and the publish is still a crash window unless an outbox row covers it.
